structured_output.world_model:
Simplest model: time ≈ fixed (~0.12 s, partly removable) + steps × per-step cost. Per-step cost is pixel-proportional plus a large memory-bound component on the 31×31 maps (whitening output and group 1: BN/GELU/pool). Accuracy rises slowly with total steps (~0.2 pp per 0.5 epoch, ~1.5–2.7 s/pp). Tip E036: 5.31 s, 0.7532 on seeds 0–2. Held-out is probably ~0.752–0.753, so headroom over the 0.75 bar is thin and the tip is close to the accuracy cliff.

Mechanisms:
1. Early low resolution is cheap (E026, E033). The 32 px tail and the 3×3 final-map regime carry accuracy (E011, E018, E024).
2. Memory-bound cuts save more than their MAC share (E028, E034, E036). The annealed group-1 LR makes the freeze nearly free in accuracy at 75%. But E037 shows the dose is nonlinear: moving the freeze to 60% cost ~0.4 pp for ~0.25 s (~0.6 s/pp, better than epochs only if epochs can't be bought back). 75% is near the knee, so deeper freezes are not free.
3. Averaging, LS and warmup tweaks (E025, E029, E030, E032) are null or negative, by 0.2–0.7 pp. The recipe sits at a local optimum with many knobs tuned in a narrow basin, so "time-neutral boosters" mostly fail.
4. wd ×0.5 helped ~0.2 pp (E016). Muon's gain is confounded with batch size and an RNG re-draw (E006).
5. Systems work is worth ~1% each (CUDA graphs E015, prepare cost E035). Remaining levers are small, ≲0.1 s each.
6. Sample dropping (E031) costs ~0.4 pp for ~0.5 s, worse than the epoch dial.

Noise: 3-seed accuracy SE ~0.1–0.15 pp. Held-out 10-seed SE ~0.06 pp. Time noise ±0.03 s. Any RNG change re-rolls seeds 0–2. Winner's curse of ~0.05–0.1 pp on seeds 3–12.

Misses: I underestimated memory-bound savings, and I overestimated accuracy tolerance of the deeper freeze (E037) and the cost of E034 time. Accuracy tweaks keep failing, so I should shade toward ~−0.1 pp for any change that is not purely systems.

Unsure: tip held-out mean; PCIe transfer of memory-bound levers; BN-folding gains (group-1 BN in eval mode may change dynamics slightly).

forecasts.reason: Diagnostic with no recipe change; the fresh-seed mean likely sits ~0.752, near the bar. The accuracy field is the mean of the 3 default seeds if recorded, so it would match the tip.
Saves BN stats passes on the 31×31 maps for the last 25% of steps, about 0.08–0.12 s. Accuracy risk is small but real since the BN stats get frozen, and the held-out mean may not clear the keep gate.
Profiling will probably show non-GEMM kernels at ≥30% of a 32 px step, consistent with E028 and E037.
The Muon NS overhead is only ~3%, so time falls a little. Accuracy likely drops 0.3 pp or more, which would predict that Muon helps.

cruxes: Where is the accuracy knee of the freeze and the resolution schedule: is 75% already at the cliff, so that all remaining stem levers cost accuracy that must be bought back with epochs?
What is the true held-out mean of the tip (seeds 3–22)? If it is below 0.752, any further time cut forces an epoch top-up and the net gain shrinks.
What fraction of a 32 px step is non-GEMM memory-bound work after the freeze (BN folding value), and does it transfer to the PCIe judge?
